PART I: COURSE SPECIFICATION
Course Code and Name : ITE 14 - Data Structures and Algorithms Credit Units : Lecture: 2 units Laboratory: 1 unit
Pre-requisite/ Co-requisite : ITE 13 – Intermediate Programming Total Contact Hours : Lecture 36 hours Laboratory 54 hours
Effectivity : 1st Semester A.Y. 2025-2026 Learning Modality : Onsite/ Online
Learning Resources Needed : Classroom, Audio-visual, laptop, internet Outcomes-Based Evidence : At least 80% of the class get a rating of > 60% on all CO
Course Description:
:
This course develops students’ ability to design and implement efficient solutions to computing problems using fundamental data
structures and algorithmic techniques. It emphasizes the implementation of abstract data types using appropriate memory management in
C, and the analysis of algorithm efficiency using time/space complexity tools. Students build and evaluate linear and non-linear data
structures (e.g., linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, hashing-based structures) and apply searching, sorting, and selected algorithmic
paradigms (divide-and-conquer, greedy) to real-world problem scenarios through programming, testing, debugging, and technical
justification.
PART II: VISION, MISSION, Graduate Attributes, Institutional Outcomes, PEO, PO, CO
Vision Mission
A socially-engaged, digital, innovation, and entrepreneurial university excelling
globally in science, engineering and the arts by 2028
As a transformative university, CSU is a responsible steward of problem-solvers
and value creators who are driven to create a sustainable future for the region, the
nation, and beyond.
Graduate Attributes Institutional Outcomes
Caraga State University graduates manifest the virtue of a CSUAN: Competent,
Socially-engaged, Upright, Agile and Innovative, and Nurturing Leaders. The CSUAN
graduate is globally competent, lifelong learner, visionary steward, sustainability-
advocate, morally-upright, ethically critical, with integrity, adaptable to change,
innovative, has entrepreneurial mindset, and a transformative leader.
IO1. A CSUan demonstrates the core knowledge in their discipline, continuously
improving their knowledge and skills to meet the changing and complex demands of
the region and beyond.
IO2. A CSUan applies advanced expertise in addressing societal challenges and complex
situations as a transformative leader and purpose-driven steward.
IO3. A CSUan embodies and upholds the core values, philosophy, and the mission of
CSU in all aspects of their life.

1. Design, implement, test, and debug a program, based on a given specification that uses
and implements abstract data types (stacks, queues, priority queues, sets, maps) D D E I I I 1, 2, 7, 11 1, 2, 4 4, 9
2. Argue strengths and weaknesses among multiple implementations for a problem (i.e.,
on the aspects of iterative vs. recursive solutions and on the aspects of abstraction,
encapsulation, and information hiding)
D D E I I I 1, 4, 5, 7 1, 4, 6 4, 9
3. Analyze and evaluate algorithms using asymptotic notations, recurrence relations, and
the application of searching, sorting, and hashing algorithms. D D E I I I 1, 5, 7, 11 1, 4 4, 9
4. Implement non-linear data structures (trees, graphs, hashing) and demonstrate their
applications in real-world problems. D D E I I I 1, 2, 7, 11 1, 2, 4 4, 9

Grading System
The following table is used to assess student performance:
Grade Status Disposition
Grade in all course outcomes is
greater than 60%
Pass. Refer to the grading table for the equivalent
numerical grade
Average is greater than 60% but at
least 1 of the course outcomes are
with grade less than 60%
Implement intervention/ conduct removal exam/
require additional assessment. The final grade is
based on the original average.
Average is lesser than 60% but 50% or
more of the outcomes are attained.
Implement intervention/ conduct removal exam/
require additional assessment. The highest grade
obtained after passing the outcome is 3.0
More than 50% of the number of
Course Outcomes did not attain > 60%
Failed. 5.0

Class Policies and Important Reminders
● Rubrics are presented to the class or given together with the instructions for a particular Assessment. You may ask your instructor for the rubrics if they were not given
before the project-based assessment, essay, case study, etc.
● Any student found to have committed fraud, after due process, shall receive a failing grade in the course.
● Refer to the student handbook for the code of conduct inside/ outside the classroom.

● Thareja, R. Data Structures Using C. Oxford University Press.
● Srivastava, S.K., & Srivastava, D. Data Structures Through C in Depth. BPB Publications.
